column2: With one hand place your thumb on ST36, 3 finger-widths below the kneecap, to the side of the edge of the shinbone, and with the other hand place your thumb on SP6, 3 finger-widths above the ankle bone, on the back edge of the shinbone. Press both at the same time with medium, comfortable pressure (4–6/10) for 60–90 seconds.

With the pad of your thumb or index finger, press lightly to moderately (3–5/10) and make small circles; on the temples, only gently, 1–2 cm, moving the skin along with your finger. Keep a slow rhythm, about one circle per second. Change direction after 30 s if it is comfortable.
If you have known or suspected deep vein thrombosis (swollen, painful, warm, red calf), do not massage the area and seek urgent medical attention.

With one thumb on KI1, on the sole where the front third meets the middle third, and with the other thumb on KI3, in the hollow between the inner ankle bone and the Achilles tendon, press both at the same time with medium, comfortable pressure (4–6/10). Breathe slowly for 60–90 seconds, then switch feet.

With the fingertips of two fingers of one hand, press lightly on LU1, below the collarbone, level with the shoulder, and with the palm of the other hand touch CV17, on the breastbone, between the nipples, with very light pressure. Take deep breaths for 45–60 seconds, then switch sides.

If you have heart disease, hard-to-control high blood pressure or rhythm disorders, ask your doctor first.
If you have cancer, are undergoing chemotherapy or radiotherapy, or have recently finished treatment, get the approval of your medical team.
If you have diabetes with neuropathy or reduced sensation in the foot, wounds, fungal infections, blisters or heel pain, do not do this exercise without your doctor's approval.
If you have diabetes, especially with neuropathy or reduced sensation in the feet, talk to your doctor before foot massage.
If you have chest pain, difficulty breathing, sudden weakness, speech difficulties or heavy bleeding, call 112. Do not use acupressure instead of medical help.
If you have osteoporosis, a herniated disc, radicular pain or spinal conditions, get your doctor's approval.
If the pain is new, intense, does not improve within a few days or appears after an injury, you need a medical consultation, not massage.
If you take anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs or have a bleeding disorder, ask your doctor what pressure intensity is acceptable.
